subject: Political Science (Code: 323)
past_paper_reference: CUET UG Political Science Past Papers (2022-2024)

questions.question: Which radical communist slogan was raised by the Communist Party of India (CPI) during its violent insurrectionary phase in 1948 regarding India's independence?
options: A) 'Yeh azaadi jhoothi hai' (This freedom is false)
questions.explanation: Under the radical leadership of B.T. Ranadive in 1948, the CPI declared that India's national independence was an illusion ('Yeh azaadi jhoothi hai') and launched armed peasant uprisings.

questions.question: On which tragic date was Mahatma Gandhi assassinated by Nathuram Vinayak Godse during an evening prayer meeting at Birla House, New Delhi?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi was shot dead by Nathuram Godse on 30 January 1948 at Birla House, prompting the Government of India to immediately ban the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS).

questions.question: Which public law enacted by the United States Congress was used by India in the 1960s to import subsidized American wheat during the severe foodgrain crisis?
questions.explanation: India relied heavily on wheat shipments from the United States under Public Law 480 (PL-480) during the food shortages of the 1960s, creating foreign policy vulnerabilities.

questions.question: Who was the renowned Indian nuclear physicist who spearheaded India's indigenous atomic energy program and established the Atomic Energy Commission in 1948?
questions.explanation: Dr. Homi J. Bhabha was the founding father of India's nuclear program and guided the creation of the Atomic Energy Commission in August 1948.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: In which month and year did the government of Indira Gandhi nationalise 14 major private commercial banks in India through an executive ordinance?
questions.explanation: On 19 July 1969, Prime Minister Indira Gandhi nationalized 14 leading commercial banks with deposits over 50 crore rupees to direct credit toward agriculture and small industries.

questions.question: Who served as the President of India who signed the historic proclamation of National Emergency on the night of 25 June 1975?
questions.explanation: President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed signed the presidential proclamation of Emergency under Article 352 late on the night of 25 June 1975 upon Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's advice.

questions.question: On which fateful date was Prime Minister Indira Gandhi assassinated by two of her Sikh bodyguards at her official residence in New Delhi?
questions.explanation: Indira Gandhi was assassinated by her security guards Satwant Singh and Beant Singh on 31 October 1984, which was followed by widespread anti-Sikh violence across Delhi and northern India.

questions.question: In which year did the First Backward Classes Commission headed by Kaka Kalelkar submit its report to the Government of India?
questions.explanation: The First Backward Classes Commission, appointed under Article 340 in 1953 under Kaka Kalelkar, submitted its recommendations in 1955 identifying socially and educationally backward groups.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: What Russian word was coined by Mikhail Gorbachev to describe his flagship policy of economic and administrative 'restructuring'?
questions.explanation: Perestroika translates to 'restructuring' and referred to the policy introduced by Gorbachev to reform and decentralize the stagnant Soviet economic and political system.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: How many sovereign countries are currently members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)?
questions.explanation: ASEAN expanded from its 5 original founding states to 10 member states: Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Brunei, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, and Cambodia.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Which of the following multinational automobile corporations originated in South Korea and became a major competitor in the global automotive sector?
questions.explanation: Hyundai Motor Company is a flagship South Korean conglomerate that emerged as a major global carmaker during South Korea's industrial rise.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: In which armed clash in the summer of 1999 did Indian armed forces recapture strategic mountain heights in Jammu and Kashmir from Pakistani-backed infiltrators?
questions.explanation: The Kargil War was fought between May and July 1999 when Indian troops evicted Pakistani regular soldiers and infiltrators occupying high-altitude peaks in the Kargil-Drass sector.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: Where is the headquarters of the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) located?
questions.explanation: UNESCO, the specialized UN agency promoting world peace and security through international cooperation in education, sciences, and culture, is headquartered in Paris.

questions.question: Which international disarmament treaty signed in 1972 banned the development, production, and stockpiling of bacteriological (biological) weapons?
questions.explanation: The Biological Weapons Convention (BWC) was opened for signature in 1972, outlawing the development, production, and possession of biological and toxin weapons.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: The global commons in international environmental governance includes all of the following domains EXCEPT:
options: B) The ocean floor beyond national jurisdictions
C) National territorial river basins and internal lakes
questions.explanation: The 'Global Commons' are areas situated outside sovereign jurisdiction: the Earth's atmosphere, Antarctica, the deep sea bed/ocean floor, and outer space. National river basins fall under sovereign territorial jurisdiction.

questions.question: How did the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) in Mexico differ fundamentally from the Indian National Congress in maintaining its six-decade-long dominance?
options: A) The PRI completely outlawed all private property and established a Soviet-style military dictatorship
B) The PRI allowed total press freedom whereas India banned all opposition newspapers from 1952 to 1967
C) The PRI ruled without a written constitution whereas India conducted elections strictly under presidential decrees
D) The PRI routinely rigged elections, co-opted trade unions, and monopolized state machinery, whereas Congress competed in free and fair multi-party elections
questions.explanation: Unlike Mexico's PRI which used electoral manipulation, clientelism, and state coercion to stay in power for 71 years, the Indian National Congress maintained dominance through competitive democratic consensus in genuine multi-party elections.

questions.question: Which of the following regions saw intense mass protests demanding linguistic reorganisation under the banner of the 'Mahagujarat Andolan'?
options: A) The Gujarati-speaking districts of Bombay State led by Indulal Yagnik
B) The Marathi-speaking Vidarbha region led by Bapu Aney
C) The Konkan coastal districts led by Nath Pai
D) The Saurashtra princely confederacy led by U.N. Dhebar
questions.explanation: The Mahagujarat Andolan, led by Indulal Yagnik, demanded the creation of a separate Gujarat state out of bilingual Bombay state, which was achieved on 1 May 1960.

questions.question: What was the statutory objective behind the creation of the Food Corporation of India (FCI) in 1965?
options: A) To export premium basmati rice and spices exclusively to Western European nations
B) To procure foodgrains from farmers at MSP, manage national buffer stocks, and supply grains to the Public Distribution System (PDS)
C) To completely take over all privately owned agricultural farmland across India
D) To enforce mandatory collective farming along the lines of Soviet Sovkhozes
questions.explanation: The FCI was set up under the Food Corporations Act, 1964, to procure foodgrains at minimum support prices, maintain strategic national buffer stocks, and ensure food security via the PDS.

questions.question: Which international conference held in Geneva in 1954 saw India playing a prominent diplomatic role as the Chairman of the International Control Commission (ICC)?
options: A) The Paris Peace Conference on Algeria
B) The Helsinki Conference on European Security
C) The Geneva Conference on Indochina
questions.explanation: Following the 1954 Geneva Accords ending French colonial rule in Indochina, India was appointed Chairman of the International Control Commission to supervise peace in Vietnam, Laos, and Cambodia.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: In the fourth General Election of 1967, which stalwart Congress leader and former Chief Minister of Madras was defeated by a student leader of the DMK in his home constituency?
questions.explanation: Congress President K. Kamaraj suffered a shocking electoral defeat in Virudhunagar at the hands of student activist P. Seenivasan of the DMK in the 1967 elections.

questions.sub_topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: How did Prime Minister Indira Gandhi outmaneuver the conservative 'Syndicate' within the Congress prior to the 1971 elections?
options: A) By adopting a sharp left-of-centre pro-poor agenda, championing bank nationalisation, and appealing directly to the electorate over the heads of regional party bosses
B) By forging an unconditional coalition with the Swatantra Party and Jana Sangh
C) By repealing the Constitution of India and declaring presidential rule nationwide
D) By relinquishing the post of Prime Minister and working solely as Congress party president
questions.explanation: Indira Gandhi projected herself as the champion of the poor, marginalized, and minorities through populist socialist reforms (Garibi Hatao, bank nationalisation), isolating the conservative bosses.

questions.question: What was the main ground on which Justice J.L. Sinha of the Allahabad High Court unseated Indira Gandhi in June 1975?
options: A) Bribing opposition polling agents in Rae Bareli with foreign currency
B) Corrupt election practice of utilizing the services of government officers, notably Yashpal Kapur, for her election campaign
C) Tampering with electronic voting machines across Uttar Pradesh constituencies
D) Failing to disclose ancestral immovable assets to the Election Commission of India
questions.explanation: The Allahabad High Court held Indira Gandhi guilty of corrupt practices under Section 123(7) of the Representation of the People Act for obtaining the assistance of gazetted government officials in her campaign.

questions.question: Which of the following civil liberties and human rights organizations was formed in 1976 during the Emergency to defend constitutional liberties in India?
options: C) People's Union for Civil Liberties (PUCL)
questions.explanation: Jayaprakash Narayan founded the People's Union for Civil Liberties and Democratic Rights (later PUCL) in 1976 to resist state tyranny and defend civil liberties.

questions.question: Under the 1986 Mizo Accord, what was the key political compromise reached between the Union Government and the Mizo National Front (MNF)?
options: A) Mizoram was merged with the state of Assam to create an autonomous tribal district
B) Laldenga was appointed the Governor of Nagaland while MNF insurgents were integrated into the Assam Rifles
C) The Union Territory of Mizoram was ceded to Myanmar under UN supervision
D) The MNF agreed to lay down arms and abandon secession, while Mizoram was granted full statehood with special constitutional protections under Article 371G
questions.explanation: The 1986 Mizo Peace Accord granted Mizoram full statehood with special protections for customary law and religious practices under Article 371G; Laldenga took oath as Chief Minister.

questions.question: What key agreement was signed between Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and Sheikh Abdullah in November 1974?
options: A) Indira-Sheikh Accord, under which Sheikh Abdullah became Chief Minister and reaffirmed Jammu and Kashmir's accession to India
B) The Delhi Agreement granting Kashmir a separate sovereign passport and currency
C) The Tashkent Protocol transferring administrative control of Gilgit to Jammu
D) The Shimla Declaration ceding the Kashmir valley to a joint Indo-Pak condominium
questions.explanation: The 1974 Indira-Sheikh Accord reaffirmed that Jammu and Kashmir was a constituent unit of the Union of India, while Sheikh Abdullah assumed office as Chief Minister of the state.

questions.question: What specific percentage of government jobs in central services and public sector undertakings was reserved for Other Backward Classes (OBCs) by the Mandal Commission?
questions.explanation: The Mandal Commission recommended a 27% quota for OBCs so that the total reservation (including 15% for SCs and 7.5% for STs) remained below the 50% legal ceiling.

questions.question: In which landmark 1992 judgment did a nine-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court uphold the 27% OBC reservation while imposing a 50% cap on total reservations?
options: A) Minerva Mills v. Union of India
B) S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
C) Indra Sawhney v. Union of India
D) Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
questions.explanation: In Indra Sawhney (1992), known as the Mandal case, the Supreme Court upheld the constitutional validity of 27% OBC quota while introducing the 'creamy layer' exclusion and 50% ceiling.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: In August 1991, an abortive military coup to overthrow Mikhail Gorbachev was organized by which faction within the Soviet leadership?
options: A) Pro-Western liberal economists led by Boris Yeltsin
B) Radical Islamic separatists from the Central Asian republics
C) The striking dockyard workers of Poland's Solidarity movement
D) Communist Party hardliners and military officials calling themselves the State Emergency Committee
questions.explanation: A group of conservative Communist Party hardliners, KGB chiefs, and military officers staged the August 1991 coup to prevent the signing of the New Union Treaty, but collapsed within three days.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: Which of the following was a central motivation behind India maintaining close strategic relations with Russia after the collapse of the Soviet Union?
options: A) Ensuring uninterrupted supplies of advanced defense equipment, nuclear technology, and access to Central Asian energy resources
B) Joining a joint military invasion of Western European nations
C) Securing complete Russian financial subsidies to balance the Union budget
D) Reviving the Warsaw Pact under Indian administrative leadership
questions.explanation: Russia remains India's premier defense hardware partner, shares intelligence on terrorism, supports India's stance on Kashmir, and collaborates on nuclear and space technology.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Why did the European Union's attempt to adopt a formal common Constitution fail in 2005?
options: A) Because the United States imposed economic sanctions on all EU member states
B) Because it was rejected by citizens of France and the Netherlands in national referendums
C) Because the European Central Bank collapsed following the collapse of the Euro
D) Because the United Nations Security Council ruled it unconstitutional under international law
questions.explanation: The proposed Treaty establishing a Constitution for Europe was rejected by voters in referendums in France and the Netherlands in May-June 2005, forcing EU leaders to abandon it.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: What major economic policy shift did China undertake in 1982 that catalyzed tremendous growth in its rural economy?
options: A) The complete collectivization of all peasant land into military communes
B) The total abolition of all private farmer markets across rural provinces
C) Privatization of agriculture through the Household Responsibility System
D) The ban on all agricultural machinery manufactured outside China
questions.explanation: China dismantled the commune system in 1982 and introduced the Household Responsibility System, leasing state land to families who could sell surplus produce on open markets.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: The Indus Waters Treaty, which established a remarkably durable water-sharing framework between India and Pakistan, was signed in 1960 through the mediation of:
options: A) The International Court of Justice
B) The United Nations General Assembly
questions.explanation: Brokered by the World Bank, the Indus Waters Treaty was signed in Karachi in September 1960 by Indian Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and Pakistani President Ayub Khan.

questions.sub_topic: South Asia in the Post Cold War Era
questions.question: Which political party led by Khaleda Zia competed fiercely against Sheikh Hasina's Awami League in post-1991 democratic politics in Bangladesh?
questions.explanation: The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), founded by former military ruler Ziaur Rahman and later led by Begum Khaleda Zia, formed the main democratic rival to the Awami League.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: What is the primary operational mandate of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)?
options: A) To recruit peacekeeping combat troops for the UN Security Council
B) To lead and coordinate international action to protect refugees and resolve refugee problems worldwide
C) To manage international foreign exchange reserves and gold holdings
D) To arbitrate sovereign boundary disputes between neighboring nations
questions.explanation: Established by the UN General Assembly in 1950, UNHCR is mandated to safeguard the rights and well-being of refugees, asylum seekers, and stateless persons globally.

questions.question: What is the key difference between the 'narrow' and 'broad' concepts of Human Security in contemporary international politics?
options: A) The narrow concept focuses on nuclear weapons, while the broad concept focuses exclusively on conventional infantry
B) The narrow concept protects only military personnel, while the broad concept protects all civilian populations
C) The narrow concept focuses on protecting individuals from violent threats, while the broad concept encompasses freedom from hunger, disease, and poverty
D) The narrow concept applies only to North American states, while the broad concept applies exclusively to Asia
questions.explanation: Proponents of the narrow school define human security as freedom from violent threats to individuals, whereas the broad school includes structural threats like poverty, disease, and environmental disasters.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: Which international mechanism was established under the Kyoto Protocol allowing Annex I industrialized countries to earn emission reduction units by investing in green projects in developing countries?
questions.explanation: The Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) under Article 12 of the Kyoto Protocol allowed developed countries to invest in emission-reduction projects in developing nations to earn tradable carbon credits.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: In international resource geopolitics, why is the control of freshwater river basins like the Jordan, Euphrates, and Tigris a potent source of potential conflict?
options: A) Because upstream riparian states can construct dams and divert water, threatening the agricultural survival of downstream states
B) Because international law grants downstream nations the right to annex upstream mountains
C) Because the UN Charter prohibits any country from constructing hydroelectric power dams
D) Because freshwater rivers in arid regions are designated as international high seas
questions.explanation: Water disputes arise when upstream states (like Turkey or Israel) construct large dams or divert flows, drastically reducing the essential water supply of downstream riparian countries (like Syria, Iraq, or Jordan).

questions.question: How has modern information technology impacted the sovereign capability of national governments in the era of globalisation?
options: A) It has completely dissolved all national governments and replaced them with private software corporations
B) It has enhanced state capacity by providing governments with powerful surveillance, data tracking, and administrative governance capabilities
C) It has forced all sovereign states to surrender their criminal law enforcement powers to the United Nations
D) It has rendered all national armed forces and police services obsolete
questions.explanation: While globalisation restricts certain economic choices, technology has dramatically enhanced the capacity of the state to collect information about citizens, monitor borders, and enforce administrative governance.

questions.question: In the Second General Election of 1957, which independent communist-supported candidate who had spearheaded the Samyukta Maharashtra Samiti defeated the Congress candidate in Bombay city?
questions.explanation: Shripad Amrit Dange, a towering trade unionist and communist stalwart leading the Samyukta Maharashtra Samiti, secured a sweeping victory in Bombay city in the 1957 elections.

questions.question: Which of the following constitutional provisions was inserted by the 53rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1986, to incorporate special protections regarding customary law and land rights following the Mizo Accord?
questions.explanation: Article 371G was enacted in 1986 pursuant to the Mizo Accord, providing that no Act of Parliament relating to religious practices, customary law, and land ownership applies to Mizoram unless the state assembly resolves so.

questions.question: During the Third Five Year Plan (1961-1966), which agricultural development program introduced intensive technological packages across selected districts with assured irrigation, serving as the immediate precursor to the Green Revolution?
questions.explanation: The Intensive Agricultural District Programme (IADP), initiated in 1960-61 in 7 pilot districts, focused agricultural inputs (credit, fertilizers, seeds) in well-endowed areas to maximize grain output rapidly.

questions.question: During the 1971 Bangladesh crisis, which US naval strike group was dispatched by President Richard Nixon to the Bay of Bengal to intimidate India, before being deterred by Soviet naval deployments?
options: A) Carrier Strike Group 5 led by USS Midway
B) Task Force 74 led by the nuclear-powered aircraft carrier USS Enterprise
C) Seventh Fleet Carrier Division led by USS Nimitz
D) Task Force 58 led by USS Coral Sea
questions.explanation: The Nixon administration dispatched Task Force 74, headed by the aircraft carrier USS Enterprise, into the Bay of Bengal in December 1971 in a dramatic show of 'gunboat diplomacy' against India.

questions.question: In which controversial case decided in 1980 did the Supreme Court strike down Section 55 of the 42nd Amendment Act, reaffirming that Parliament's amending power under Article 368 is limited and cannot destroy the Basic Structure?
options: A) Waman Rao v. Union of India
B) I.R. Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu
C) Minerva Mills v. Union of India
D) Golaknath v. State of Punjab
questions.explanation: In Minerva Mills (1980), the Supreme Court struck down clauses (4) and (5) of Article 368 inserted by the 42nd Amendment, holding that a limited amending power is itself a basic feature of the Constitution.

questions.question: What was the name of the faction of the Naga underground movement that rejected the 1975 Shillong Accord signed by moderate NNC leaders, leading to the formation of the NSCN in 1980?
options: A) Naga Federal Army (led by Kughato Sukhai)
B) Mizo National Army (led by Biakchhunga)
C) United Liberation Front of Asom (led by Paresh Baruah)
D) National Socialist Council of Nagaland (led by Isak Chishi Swu and Thuingaleng Muivah)
questions.explanation: Isak Chishi Swu, Thuingaleng Muivah, and S.S. Khaplang repudiated the 1975 Shillong Accord as a capitulation and formed the NSCN in 1980 to wage a guerrilla war for a greater Nagaland.

questions.question: Which political scientist coined the phrase 'Second Democratic Upsurge' to describe the massive electoral participation and political ascendancy of the backward castes and Dalits in India during the 1990s?
questions.explanation: Yogendra Yadav conceptualized the 'Second Democratic Upsurge' in Indian politics to explain how marginalized social strata (OBCs, Dalits, rural poor) dramatically mobilized to capture political power in the 1990s.

questions.sub_topic: Disintegration of the 'Second World' and the Collapse of Bipolarity
questions.question: Which international peace agreement signed in Paris in December 1995 officially ended the 3.5-year Bosnian War, establishing a decentralized state divided into two constituent entities?
questions.explanation: The Dayton Accords, negotiated at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Dayton, Ohio, ended the Bosnian conflict and divided Bosnia and Herzegovina into the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Republika Srpska.

questions.sub_topic: Alternative Centers of Economic and Political Power
questions.question: Which of the following describes the 'Four Modernisations' articulated by Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai in 1973 and implemented by Deng Xiaoping?
options: A) Modernisation of banking, stock markets, internet infrastructure, and tourism
B) Modernisation of nuclear warheads, ballistic submarines, cyber warfare, and aerospace
C) Modernisation of agriculture, industry, national defense, and science & technology
D) Modernisation of rural cooperatives, ideological education, state monopolies, and cinema
questions.explanation: The Four Modernisations focused specifically on four key sectors: Agriculture, Industry, National Defense, and Science & Technology, transforming China into an economic superpower.

questions.sub_topic: International Organisations in a Unipolar World
questions.question: What is the specialized function of the IAEA's 'Safeguards System' established under Article III of the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT)?
options: A) Managing the global export cartel for enriched uranium to ensure fixed pricing
B) Commanding international nuclear rapid-response battalions during regional skirmishes
C) Financing the construction of coal-fired thermal power stations across developing countries
D) Verifying that non-nuclear-weapon states do not divert civilian nuclear materials to nuclear weapons or explosive devices
questions.explanation: IAEA safeguards comprise technical inspection and verification measures to ensure that fissile materials in peaceful civil nuclear programs are not diverted into military weapon development.

questions.question: Which international convention adopted in Paris in January 1993 entered into force in 1997, completely banning the production, acquisition, and stockpiling of chemical weapons?
questions.explanation: The Chemical Weapons Convention (CWC) established the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) in The Hague, requiring member states to destroy all stockpiles of chemical arms.

questions.sub_topic: Environment and Natural Resources in Global Politics
questions.question: In which landmark international declaration adopted in September 2007 did the UN General Assembly recognize the rights of indigenous peoples to self-determination, lands, territories, and cultural traditions?
options: A) Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR)
B) Rio Declaration on Environment and Development
C) Vienna Declaration and Programme of Action
D) United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP)
questions.explanation: UNDRIP was adopted by the UN General Assembly on 13 September 2007, setting minimum global standards for the survival, dignity, and well-being of the world's indigenous peoples.
